action_items: React warning during chat poll: 'Cannot update a component (JobPage) while rendering a different component (JobChat)' — indicates a setState call inside render/parent-render phase in JobChat.jsx. Not user-visible, but should be wrapped in useEffect / event handler to be strict-mode safe.
critical_code_review_comments: backend routes.py `_fetch_messages`: parses `after` with `datetime.fromisoformat(after.replace('Z','+00:00'))` and silently ignores parse failures. This is intentional per spec, but note that if a client fails to URL-encode the '+' in the ISO offset (e.g. hand-crafted curl), the server sees a space, parse fails, and every poll returns the ENTIRE history — bandwidth risk under high message volume. Frontend uses encodeURIComponent/axios params so this is not hit in the app, but consider a fallback `after.replace(' ', '+')` before fromisoformat as belt-and-braces.

`_public_job_dict`: `customer_name` is returned to anyone with the share token. Fine (customer is looking at their own delivery), but worth remembering it's PII exposed by a URL fragment — the share_token is 20 chars of urlsafe token (secrets.token_urlsafe(18)[:20]) which is ~120 bits; adequate.
`_resolve_preset` uses `sender == 'driver'` branch selection — good server-side canonicalisation prevents cross-role preset abuse (confirmed: customer sending 'downstairs' returns 400).

`share_token` generation uses `secrets.token_urlsafe(18)[:20]` — truncating a urlsafe token is fine but the slice can produce '-'/'_' chars; make sure URL routing is not confused by this in any middleware (verified 200 responses in tests).
JobChat.jsx (P2): the React warning 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' suggests a setState call inside a render path — move to useEffect. Non-blocking.
